newsitem.title: USA: Police to interview parents of murdered child.
newsitem.headline: Police to interview parents of murdered child.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of 6-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey said on Monday they hoped to set up a formal interview with the girl's parents, but would not label them as suspects.
"There are no named suspects and no arrests pending," said Boulder police spokesman Kelvin McNeill.

Police submitted written questions to the parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, the couple's spokesman said. "The answers are being prepared," Pat Korten said in a telephone interview from Washington D.C.

Police were trying to work out a schedule for a formal interview with the parents, who returned to Colorado on Friday from Georgia, where they had buried the girl. The Ramseys lived in the Atlanta, Georgia, area before moving to Boulder in 1991.

Korten said they "want to be as cooperative (with the police) as is humanly possible." But he said in a case where the parents might still be considered "possible suspects" attorneys have a duty to protect their clients.

The girl's body was found the day after Christmas in her family's 15-room home in a posh neighbourhood of Boulder, 30 miles (50 km) northwest of Denver, about eight hours after her mother had phoned police to say she had discovered a ransom note demanding $118,000.
The blond, blue-eyed child was strangled. According to news reports her skull was fractured and she was sexually assaulted, but police remained tight-lipped about aspects of the investigation.

Three of five detectives sent to Georgia to interview family and business associates returned to Colorado on Sunday night to confer with Boulder police. The remaining two were expected back on Monday night.

The Ramseys and their 9-year-old son, Burke, appeared in Boulder on Sunday to attend a memorial service for the girl at a local church. The parents gave an extensive interview to CNN last week, but otherwise have remained in seclusion.
Counsellors were on hand on Monday at JonBenet's school to talk to her classmates on their first day back from winter vacation.
The little girl had been crowned Little Miss Colorado and participated in other beauty pageants.
